correctness.rationale: For the stated real two-pole sequence, the binomial theorem gives exactly \(b_n=\beta^n\sin(n\phi)\) and \(c_n=(-1)^{n+1}\beta^n\sin(n\phi)\), while the normalized numerator limsup is one. Thus the witness ratio is \(1/L(\phi)\), where \(L(\phi)=\limsup |\sin(n\phi)|\). Irrational rotation gives \(L=1\); for \(\phi/\pi=p/q\) reduced, multiplication by \(p\) permutes residues modulo \(q\), giving \(L=1\) for even \(q\) and \(L=\cos(\pi/(2q))\) for odd \(q\). Bouthat's full theorem was read and confirms the same normalization and universal upper constant \(2/\sqrt3\).

final_claim: For fixed \(\beta>1\), with \(\alpha=\sqrt{\beta^2-1}\) and \(\phi=\arccos(1/\beta)\), the canonical two-pole witness gives \(\kappa(\beta)\ge\Gamma(\beta)\), where \(\Gamma(\beta)=\sec(\pi/(2q))\) when \(\phi/\pi\) has odd reduced denominator \(q\), and \(\Gamma(\beta)=1\) for irrational angle or even reduced denominator; together with Bouthat's universal theorem, \(\Gamma(\beta)\le\kappa(\beta)\le2/\sqrt3\), and the largest resonance is the \(q=3\), \(\beta=2\) case.
limitations: This is an exact lower profile for the canonical two-pole witness, not a determination of the true fixed-parameter constant except at \(\beta=2\).
Other sequence families may yield stronger fixed-parameter lower bounds.
